text: You flush a toilet every day. Does it push the waste down, or pull it? Most people guess wrong.
It pulls. Press the handle, and a chain lifts a rubber flapper. The whole tank rushes into the bowl.
Water floods in faster than the drain can swallow it, so the level rises and fills a curved pipe hidden in the base.
The instant that curve is full, a siphon starts. Gravity pulls the long side down, air pressure pushes from behind, and the bowl is dragged away in seconds.
Then comes the gurgle. Air sneaks in, the siphon breaks, and the water left behind seals out sewer gas.
Meanwhile the tank refills, and a float shuts the valve when it's full.
Quick test. You hear water running after every flush. Is it the flapper, the float, or the chain? Think!
It's usually the flapper. A worn rubber seal lets the tank leak, so the valve keeps refilling it.
Proof: drop food coloring in the tank and wait ten minutes. Color in the bowl means a leak that can waste hundreds of gallons a day.
The fix is a ten dollar flapper. Check the chain has a little slack, too.
Watch again, and follow the rubber duck.
